chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, on the authority of Al-Fadl ibn Sulayman al-Kufi, on the authority of Khalid, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) say

The Sublime God has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing and All-Seeing. I asked him, 'O son of the Prophet of God! There are some people who say that God has always been All-Knowing with Knowledge, All-Powerful with His Might, Ever-Living with His Life, Ever-Lasting with His Past, and All-Hearing with His Hearing, All-Seeing with His Sight.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Whoever says this and believes in it has indeed associated other gods as partners with God. He is not under our Mastery at all.' He (peace be upon him) then added, 'The Honorable the Exalted God has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing and All-Seeing by His own High Nature. High indeed is He Exalted above what the polytheists say and the similitude they draw.'

key_terms.وَالْمُشَبَّهُونَ: and the Similitude-drawers (those who compare God to creation)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God's attributes and His essence according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the Mu'tazili view of attributes as distinct entities and the Shia doctrine of 'attributes of essence' (Sifat al-Dhat), where God's knowledge and power are identical to His very being. He warns that treating attributes as separate 'things' introduces a form of shirk by creating duality within the Divine, thereby affirming God's absolute transcendence above the anthropomorphic descriptions of polytheists and the rationalist categorizations of the Mushabbihah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-10 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il al-Barmaki, on the authority of Al-Fadhl ibn Soleiman al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Khalid: I heard Al-Ridha (s) say, “The Sublime God has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing and All-Seeing.”

I asked him, “O son of the Prophet of God! There are some people who say that God has always been All-Knowing with Knowledge, All-Powerful with His Might, Ever-Living with His Life, Ever-Lasting with His Past, and All-Hearing with His Hearing, All-Seeing with His Sight.” The Imam (s) said, “Whoever says this and believes in it has indeed associated other gods as partners with God. He is not under our Mastery at all.” He (s) then added, “The Honorable the Exalted God has always been All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Ever-Living, Ever-Lasting, All-Hearing and All-Seeing by His own High Nature. High indeed is He Exalted above what the polytheists say and the similitude they draw.”
